Graduate Application Useful Information
Frequently Asked Questions
Required Application Materials for all applicants
All applications require a resume, personal statement, transcripts, and three letters of recommendation
Personal statements should explain your motivation for graduate study
PhD and research-oriented MS applicants should also discuss areas of research and specify potential faculty advisors of interest
GRE general test scores are not required for our graduate program. You may still submit them if you feel they strengthen your application
Transcripts must show all courses taken, credit hours, and final grades. A degree certification is not sufficient.
Unofficial transcripts may be submitted at the time of application, but official transcripts are needed for final admission
Please see the individual sections below for more information, including language exam requirements
Ph.D. Applicants
Applications to the Ph.D. program received by January 15th can be considered for fellowships and assistantships that include full stipend and full tuition remission.
All admitted full-time Ph.D. students receive funding through either teaching assistantships (TA), graduate assistantships (GA) or fellowships and can expect funding for at least five years subject to satisfactory progress. TA and GA positions are reserved for Ph.D. students, and we only hold a Fall admissions cycle for Ph.D. admissions.
Our program is a hub for an NIH sponsored Biotechnology training program, a Colgate-Palmolive experiential learning opportunity program, and an NSF REU in Advanced Materials (https://cbe.rutgers.edu/research/research-traineeships) as well as centers in Pharmaceutical Engineering and Catalyst manufacture (https://cbe.rutgers.edu/research/research-centers-and-labs)
Rutgers University fosters diversity through several special fellowship and training programs and encourages applications from students with backgrounds underrepresented in chemical engineering and academia.
More information about our Ph.D. program
Submit your application
Master's Applicants
We offer two Master's degrees
Master of Science (M.S.) in Chemical and Biochemical Engineering
Master of Engineering (M.E.) in Pharmaceutical Engineering
Application to the Master’s program is done on a rolling basis. We offer both Fall and Spring admissions cycles. The application deadline is August 1st for Fall admissions and December 1st for Spring admissions. International applicants should submit their applicants earilier than this to allow for visa processing time by at least two months.
A number of our Master’s students seek out and find paid positions on campus on their own, including as graders, learning assistants, and part-time lecturers. Departments such as Chemistry, Math and Physics serve a large undergraduate population and routinely recruit CBE Master’s students for such positions. We also have a number of grader positions in our department, depending on course enrollment.
Many of our Master’s students have been successful in obtaining summer internships/co-ops in the relevant chemical or pharmaceutical industries, which can be accommodated in the form of CPT (curricular practical training) for international students.

Bachelor's/Master's or 4+1 program Applicants
Current Rutgers-New Brunswick students and recent alumni should apply for our Master's degrees through our BS/Master's program. Details can be found on the program website.
International Applicants and Language Requirement
US citizens and permanents residents and international applicants with a minimum of three years undergraduate studies or a master’s degree with the mode of instruction being English are exempt from submitting language test scores. Your scores must be current within 2 years of the semester you are applying to.
Minimum TOEFL score (tested through January 21, 2026): Writing 22, Speaking 23, Reading 21, Listening 17.
Minimum TOEFL score (tested after January 21, 2026): Writing 4.5, Speaking 4.5, Reading 4, Listening 4.
TOEFL institution code to submit scores is 2790
Minimum IELTS score is bandwidth 7
Minimum Duolingo English Test score is 120.
CBE does not manage the language exam, it is managed by the School of Graduate Studies (SGS).
For more information for international applicants, see information from Graduate Admissions here
Our international student program is supported by Rutgers Global–International Student and Scholar Services (ISSS)
Applicants Without a Degree in Chemical Engineering
The Graduate Program in Chemical and Biochemical Engineering regularly welcomes students with diverse educational backgrounds into our department for advanced study. More information can be found here.
Part-time Study and Non-Matriculated/Non-Degree (NOD) Study
All US citizens and permanent residents are eligible for part-time study and non-matriculated/non-degree study.
Part-time study is very popular with many of our Master's students who are employed full-time in local industry. Most of our graduate courses are offered in the evening which makes it convenient for part-time students to take one or two classes per semester.
Non-matriculated/non-degree study is an option to take up to four courses without being enrolled in a graduate degree program. After completing four courses, a student must then enroll in a degree program should they wish to continue study. All coursework previously completed is transferred to the degree at that point
Application Fee Information
The application fee is managed by the Office of Graduate Admissions, and not by CBE. CBE can not give out a fee waiver, but Graduate Admissions has given the following information about waivers at this link.
Fee waivers are granted to active U.S. Military and Military Veterans who plan to apply for educational benefits under the GI Bill, Rutgers alumni, and participants in certain scholar programs, such as McNair. You will be automatically reviewed for fee waiver eligibility based on the information you provide on your application.
The FreeApp Program provides fee waivers for Ph.D. program applicants at Rutgers who meet these criteria. FreeApp is a collaborative program for students traditionally underrepresented in graduate education, including racial and ethnic minorities, women in STEM, first-generation college students, and individuals who have faced adversity, such as societal, economic, or academic disadvantages.
Application fee waivers are not granted for any conditions outside those listed above.
